transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi. Well, I'm here because... for the past year, I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. No matter how many doctors or family members tell me his numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. I draw blood for a living, so I know how these things work and what I'm looking at. It's just... nobody will listen to me, and trying to get to the bottom of it is really wearing me down.

When the doctors and your family tell you that your dad's lab results are normal, do you think there's any possibility they might be right, or are you completely certain that the results are being changed?

No, there isn't any possibility they're right. I'm completely certain. Like I said, I've spent this entire past year trying to prove that someone in the system is changing or holding back parts of his results. It doesn't matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine... I know the chart doesn't match what I saw. I wouldn't be letting this wear me down so much if I had any doubts about it.
Does your dad also believe that someone is changing or holding back his lab results, or is this something that only you are convinced about?

No, it's just me. He doesn't really question it... he just listens to whatever the doctors tell him. I'm the only one who actually knows how to read the labs and sees what's going on, so I'm the one trying to fix it.

You mentioned that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back your dad's lab results. Can you tell me specifically who you believe is doing this? Do you know which person or people are responsible?

I honestly don't know. I mean... I don't have a specific name. If I knew exactly who was doing it, I would have reported them by now. I just know it's happening somewhere in the system—maybe someone in medical records, or whoever enters the data into the charts. But no, I don't know the exact person responsible. I just know what I'm seeing.

When you think about who might be changing your dad's lab results, do you believe there's a particular person or group of people who have a reason or motivation to do this to you or your family specifically?

I really don't know. I've tried to figure that out... you know, if someone has a grudge against my dad or our family. But no, I can't think of any reason why they would target us specifically. We don't have enemies or anything like that. 

I don't know what their motivation is at all. Maybe they're just trying to cover up some kind of mistake they made in the lab, or maybe it's something else entirely... I honestly don't know the "why." I just know it's happening.

Over this past year, when did you first start noticing that the lab results didn't match what you saw? Did this belief develop gradually over time, or did it suddenly become clear to you at a specific point?

It started about a year ago. That's when my dad's medical problems really kicked up and he started needing frequent labs and going to all these appointments. I'd say it became pretty clear to me as soon as I started looking at the results coming back. Since I know what to look for, I noticed right away that things weren't matching up with what I was seeing. So yeah, it's been going on for a solid year now.

When you think about these lab results being changed or held back, do you believe someone is deliberately doing this to harm you or your family, or do you think it's more about someone trying to hide a mistake they made?

I honestly don't know for sure. I mean... I don't think it's about harming us on purpose. Like I said earlier, we don't have enemies or anyone who would want to target my dad like that. 

It makes a lot more sense that someone just messed up—maybe they ran the sample wrong or contaminated it, or lost the original data—and now they're just trying to cover their tracks so they don't get in trouble or lose their job. But... I can't say that with a hundred percent certainty because I'm not the one doing it. I don't know their actual motive. I just know what the results are supposed to look like, and what they're putting in his chart isn't right.

When you look back over this past year, have you been able to piece together a logical explanation for how this is happening—like, a step-by-step process of how someone would change the results or cover them up? Or does it feel more like you just know something is wrong without being able to explain exactly how they're doing it?

I don't really have a step-by-step theory for how they're doing it. I mean, I work in a lab setting, so I know there are ways data can be altered in the system before it gets finalized in the chart, but I haven't been able to piece together exactly how they are pulling it off in my dad's case. 

I just know what I'm looking at. When I draw his blood and see the physical state of the sample, and then I look at the numbers they report back... they just don't match. I don't know the exact process they're using to change it, I just know that the end result is wrong.

When you look at your dad's lab results in the chart and compare them to what you remember seeing or what you expect them to be, do you actually see different numbers written down, or is it more that you're calculating what the numbers should be based on your knowledge of labs?

I don't really sit there and calculate an exact number, if that's what you mean. It's not a math equation. And I'm not seeing the numbers magically change on the screen or anything like that. 

I just read the final numbers they posted in his chart, and I know they're incorrect. Like, because of my job, if I draw his blood and I can physically see the sample is hemolyzed or lipemic, I know how that's supposed to affect the results. But then I look at the chart, and the numbers they put in the system just... they don't reflect that at all. They'll just be totally normal. So I'm not calculating the exact digits in my head, I just know the numbers they actually wrote down aren't the right ones for the blood I drew.

If we brought in an independent lab expert to review your dad's blood samples and the reported results, and they told you everything was normal and there was no evidence of tampering, would you be able to accept that conclusion, or would you still believe the results had been altered?

I don't think I could accept that. I mean... for the past year, I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. And already, no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, it doesn't change anything for me. 

I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. So if you brought in another expert and they said everything was normal, I'd still believe the results were altered. I wouldn't be able to just agree with them. It's just... it's really wearing me down, honestly, constantly being told I'm wrong when I know exactly what I'm looking at.

You mentioned that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back your dad's lab results. When you think about how they might be doing this—like, are we talking about someone physically altering the blood sample itself, or changing the numbers in the computer system after the fact, or something else entirely? What would be the most likely way they're actually doing it?

I don't really know exactly how they're doing it. I mean, I don't think they're physically messing with the blood tubes after I draw them. It's got to be something in the computer system. 

Like I said before, I know there are ways to alter data before it gets finalized. So maybe they're just typing in different numbers, or maybe there's some kind of block on certain results so they just don't show up in the chart. I honestly couldn't tell you the exact mechanics of it. I just know what I see when I draw the blood, and I know what ends up in the system isn't right.

When you think about someone changing your dad's lab results in the computer system, do you believe this is something that could realistically happen using normal computer access and methods that exist in a typical medical facility, or does it seem like it would require something unusual or impossible?

I mean, I don't think it's anything impossible. It's just a computer system. People who work in the lab or IT have access to change things or override results all the time. That's just how the software works in a normal clinic. So it doesn't take some kind of super hacker or magic trick. It's just someone with the right login going in and altering the numbers before they get posted to his chart. It's completely realistic for a medical facility.

Beyond the concern about your dad's lab results being changed, do you have other beliefs or concerns about things happening to you or your family—like people following you, listening to your conversations, or other ways people might be interfering with your life or your dad's care?

No, I don't have anything like that happening. Nobody is following me or listening to my calls or anything. It's really just the lab results. I mean, that's the only thing I'm focused on because that's what I know is wrong. I don't have any reason to think anyone is interfering with my life in other ways, or doing anything else to my dad's care. It's just the numbers in the system.

You've said you're completely certain the lab results are being changed. But if you really think about it honestly, is there any small part of you that wonders if maybe you could be misinterpreting what you're seeing—even if it seems unlikely to you?

No, honestly, there isn't. I mean, I understand why you would ask that, but I'm not misinterpreting anything. 

For the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. And no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine and that I must be mistaken, I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw. I just know it. 

It’s... it's really wearing me down, having to constantly defend what I know is true when nobody else will look at the facts. But no, I don't have any doubts about what I'm seeing.

When you look at your dad's lab results in the chart and compare them to what you saw or remember, can you walk me through one specific example—like, what was the test name, what did you observe about the blood sample, and what numbers appeared in the chart that didn't match?

I mean, I don't really have a specific example like that. It's not about the color of the blood or anything I observed when they drew it. I'm a phlebotomist, so I know how the blood looks doesn't tell you the numbers. It's just... when I look at the chart, the numbers aren't right. I don't have one specific test name or exact number to give you right now, but I know what I'm looking at, and I know they've been altered. It's the whole picture of his results that just doesn't add up to what it should be.

You've been focused on your dad's lab results for a year now. In that time, have you developed any other beliefs about what might be going wrong with his medical care—like problems with his medications, his diagnoses, or how the doctors are treating him—or is it really just the lab results that concern you?

No, it's really just the lab results. I haven't noticed anything weird with his medications or... or how the doctors are treating him in general. His diagnoses make sense to me. 

It's literally just the numbers in the system. I'm not trying to find problems with his whole care plan or anything like that. The doctors are doing their jobs fine with the treatment part. I just want the chart to actually reflect his real lab work. That's the only thing I'm concerned about, because that's the only thing that's being altered.

You mentioned that when you look at your dad's blood sample and then look at the chart numbers, they don't match up. But I want to understand this better—are you saying that you actually have access to see his original lab results or blood samples side-by-side with what's in the chart, or are you comparing what you remember from seeing the blood to what you see in the chart later?

I think you misunderstood what I said earlier. I'm a phlebotomist, so I know you can't just look at a vial of blood and know what the numbers are going to be. That's not what I'm doing. 

I don't have the original lab reports sitting in front of me to compare side-by-side with the chart, either. If I did, I wouldn't be having this problem, because I could just show everyone the proof. 

It's just that when I look at his chart in the system, I know the numbers have been changed. I know what his results should look like, and the ones in the system are wrong. They're just... they're not the real results. I don't know how else to explain it, but I'm not comparing a tube of blood to a computer screen. I just know the chart is altered.

Besides the belief about your dad's lab results being changed, do you have any other strong beliefs about things that are happening—for example, beliefs that people are trying to harm you, that you're being monitored or controlled, or that there are hidden meanings in everyday events—or is the lab result issue really the only thing you're preoccupied with?

No, I don't have any beliefs like that. Nobody is monitoring me or trying to harm me, and there aren't any hidden meanings in things. It really is just the lab results. 

I'm basically just here because for the past year, I've been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad's lab results. And no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn't match what I saw. It's just... it's really wearing me down, honestly, trying to get people to see it. But no, nothing else like what you're asking about. Just the labs.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a circumscribed, non-bizarre delusional belief (lab results being altered) that has persisted for approximately one year. The delusion is held with absolute conviction despite contradictory evidence from multiple credible sources (doctors, family members, independent experts). Importantly, the delusion remains isolated to this single theme without extension to other domains (no beliefs about surveillance, harm, or hidden meanings). The patient demonstrates functional impairment (preoccupation causing distress and wearing her down) but retains relatively preserved functioning otherwise. The absence of prominent hallucinations, negative symptoms, or disorganization, combined with the circumscribed nature of the delusion and duration >1 month, is most consistent with Delusional Disorder, Somatic Type (F22.0), rather than Brief Psychotic Disorder or other psychotic disorders.
